title: The Contract Act, 1872
verification_note: Section summaries checked against official online Act on 2026-10-20; current consolidated legal status and amendments require editorial verification.

sections.heading: What agreements are contracts
sections.explanation: Section 10 generally requires free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration, a lawful object, and no express statutory declaration of voidness. Other laws may require writing, witnesses or registration.
sections.example: If two competent adults freely agree to buy and sell lawful goods for an agreed price, the basic contractual elements may be present; other applicable statutory requirements must still be checked.

sections.heading: Who are competent to contract
sections.explanation: Contractual capacity depends on the age of majority under applicable law, soundness of mind, and absence of legal disqualification.
sections.example: A purported contract signed by a person lacking legal capacity must be examined for enforceability before relying on it.

sections.heading: Lawful consideration and object
sections.explanation: An agreement's purpose or consideration may be unlawful if forbidden by law, fraudulent, harmful, or contrary to public policy under this provision.
sections.example: A promise to pay someone for a prohibited act does not become enforceable merely because both parties sign a document.

sections.heading: Agreement without consideration
sections.explanation: Section 25 states a general rule that agreements without consideration are void, subject to specified exceptions that must be checked in the section text.
sections.example: A promise to make a gift without anything in return may not create an enforceable contract unless a statutory exception applies.
